**Definition:** Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.
catalogue domains below are explicitly **CT1 roots**; each branch statement

HCM-BC-individual-care-delivery.governed_definition_latex: Assess, clinically determine, plan, intervene, monitor and review individual care independently of setting, mode, time pattern or organisational arrangement.

sources.text: ##### 01.01 Individual Health Assessment
**Tier and ancestry:** CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
##### CT2 — Individual Health Assessment
**Definition:** Establish an understanding of an individual’s current health state.

**Boundary:** The decomposition distinguishes means of establishing knowledge. Functional, nutritional, cognitive, mental-health and similar labels are assessment domains, not automatically peer abilities. Risk interpretation belongs to Clinical Determination. Care setting, profession, specialty and information type do not define the decomposition.

HCM-BC-individual-health-assessment.governed_definition_latex: The capability to establish an understanding of an individual's current health state through the collection, consideration and evaluation of relevant clinical, health and contextual information.

sources.text: ##### 01.02 Clinical Determination
**Tier and ancestry:** CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).

HCM-BC-clinical-determination.governed_definition_latex: The capability to interpret assessed health information and establish clinically meaningful conclusions about an individual's health state, condition, risk or prognosis.

sources.text: ##### 01.03 Individual Care Planning
**Tier and ancestry:** CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).

HCM-BC-individual-care-planning.governed_definition_latex: The capability to establish the intended clinical response to an individual's assessed and clinically interpreted health state, including the objectives, interventions and monitoring required to progress their care.

sources.text: ##### 01.04 Clinical Intervention
**Tier and ancestry:** CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).

HCM-BC-clinical-intervention.governed_definition_latex: The capability to perform clinical actions intended to alter, maintain or otherwise manage an individual's health state in accordance with an established care intent.

sources.text: ##### 01.05 Individual Health Monitoring
**Tier and ancestry:** CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
##### CT2 — Individual Health Monitoring
**Definition:** Observe health over time to identify change, stability or deviation.

**Boundary:** Care Response Monitoring consumes health-state services provided through Health State Monitoring without independently recreating the aggregate view. This semantic consumption establishes no named Service, interface or runtime invocation. Measurement supplies observations; monitoring establishes a view; Clinical Determination interprets its clinical significance. Deterioration, improvement and stability are possible monitored states, not established peer CT3s.

HCM-BC-individual-health-monitoring.governed_definition_latex: The capability to observe and evaluate an individual's health state over time in order to identify clinically meaningful change, stability or deviation from an expected state or trajectory.

sources.text: ##### 01.06 Individual Care Review
**Tier and ancestry:** CT2; parent Individual Care Delivery (CT1).
##### CT2 — Individual Care Review
**Definition:** Evaluate care against intent and objectives.

**Boundary:** An effectiveness finding may inform appropriateness without replacing it. Care may be appropriate yet ineffective, or effective yet no longer appropriate to continue. Monitoring the response is distinct from judging effectiveness; identifying a need to reconsider care does not establish the replacement plan. Replanning belongs to Individual Care Planning.

HCM-BC-individual-care-review.governed_definition_latex: The capability to evaluate the progress and effectiveness of an individual's care against its intended objectives and establish the continuing appropriateness of the current care intent.

#### Design Service Assurance

HCM-FN-design-service-assurance.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Design Service Assurance}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Defines how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be independently established, including the applicable assurance disposition, assurance criteria, required evidence and evaluation expectations.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Concerns assurance design. It does not establish the underlying governance requirement, grant authority to it, perform the resulting assurance, manage the subject activity or prescribe application or implementation mechanisms. Modelling the resulting Assurance Definition does not grant approval authority. The Strategy peer relationship to behaviour design and failure/\allowbreak{}recovery design creates no additional Capability or Function.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: #### Manage Assurance Criteria

HCM-FN-manage-assurance-criteria.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Manage Assurance Criteria}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Establishes and manages reusable, governed and temporally identifiable assurance criteria through which governed subjects may be evaluated.



\item 
\textbf{Scope}: Criteria may express governance rule boundaries, quality constraints, performance expectations, compliance criteria, temporal criteria, evidence requirements or completeness expectations. These examples are not an exhaustive taxonomy. Criteria may have lifecycle, version and temporal applicability.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Managing a criterion does not transfer authority for the governing requirement from which it may derive. Criteria may operationalise a requirement without silently altering, weakening, strengthening or replacing it; not every criterion must derive from formal Governance. Modelling/\allowbreak{}managing criteria does not inherently confer approval authority. Detailed criterion lifecycle states and approval workflows remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: #### Establish Assurance Context

HCM-FN-establish-assurance-context.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Establish Assurance Context}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Establishes the governed subject, applicable assurance purpose and criteria, relevant temporal context, and contextual association of sufficient trustworthy source information as evidence required for an assurance activity.



\item 
\textbf{Scope}: Includes the evidence-assembly responsibility previously described as Assurance Evidence Assembly; no separate evidence-assembly Function is established. Sufficiency is required for conclusion, not assumed merely because context is established; unavailable or insufficient evidence remains explicit.



\item 
\textbf{Information Boundary}: Source information remains owned by its responsible source Capability. Its use as evidence does not transfer ownership or originating authority. Governed Assurance owns the contextual association that particular information constitutes evidence for a particular assurance purpose. Evidence association and applicable criteria may each be temporal and version-specific; association distinguishes the information state relevant to assurance from its current state.



\item 
\textbf{Realisation Boundary}: Uses generic EC-02 context-management capability together with EC-14 assurance-specific semantics as documented in \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#41-context-management-contribution}{§4.1}. Establishment of Assurance Context prescribes no copying, persistence, aggregation, caching or other technical mechanism.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### 5.1 Request Service Assurance

HCM-SV-request-service-assurance.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Request Service Assurance}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Enables an authorised consumer to request that Service Assurance be performed for an applicable governed subject in accordance with an established Assurance Definition.



\item 
\textbf{Approved Consumers}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Care Coordinator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Service Coordinator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Regulator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Policy Authority}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{System Steward}}.



\item 
\textbf{Associated Interaction}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-request}{Service Assurance Request}, with Service Guardian and one authorised requesting Role.



\item 
\textbf{Process Relationship}: Requests \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md\#assurance-process-execution}{Assurance Process Execution} under an applicable established Assurance Definition. It does not require a new Assurance Process Design instance for each request.



\item 
\textbf{Independence Boundary}: The requesting Role identifies the assurance need within its responsibility and authority. Requesting does not grant authority to define or alter the Assurance Definition, alter Assurance Criteria, direct evidence assessment, determine adjudication or control the resulting Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion. REQ-FND-005 control independence remains applicable, including where a requester performs or manages the subject. Detailed payloads, contracts, initiation mechanics and states remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### 5.2 Request Service Assurance Status

HCM-SV-request-service-assurance-status.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Request Service Assurance Status}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Enables the System Steward to obtain the current business progression state of an identifiable Service Assurance activity for stewardship purposes.



\item 
\textbf{Only Approved Consumer}: \texttt{\seqsplit{System Steward}}.



\item 
\textbf{Associated Interaction}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-status}{Service Assurance Status}, between System Steward and Service Guardian.



\item 
\textbf{Status Boundary}: Concerns \textbf{activity progression state}. It does not communicate provisional findings, incomplete assessment results as conclusions, predicted outcomes or unadjudicated conclusions. Other requesting Roles do not gain status access merely because they requested assurance. No detailed activity-status taxonomy is established.



\end{itemize}

\textbf{Service Assurance Status answers "where is the assurance activity in its progression?" It does not answer "what has the assurance established?"} The latter requires an adjudicated Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion and subsequent outcome communication; neither status nor execution completion establishes that conclusion.


\textbf{Management Monitoring evaluates activity state in order to progress or manage activity. Assurance evaluates activity against governing criteria in order to establish an assurance conclusion.} System Steward's use of this Service is stewardship /\allowbreak{} management observation of assurance progression, not itself assurance or recursive assurance. The non-recursion boundary in §7.2 applies.

\item

\item

\item

A particular outcome may be communicated to one, some or all legitimate recipients according to applicability, authority, responsibility and information requirements. sources.text: ### 2.1 Governed Person Identity Correction Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Person Identity` (under `Client Administration`)

HCM-PR-governed-person-identity-correcti.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Person Identity}} (under \texttt{\seqsplit{Client Administration}})



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Processes externally authoritative identity corrections and merge/\allowbreak{}unlink outcomes, applies their consequences to Harmonia-managed identity information and identifier associations, and communicates resulting changes with an audit history.



\item 
\textbf{Authority boundary}: Person correction/\allowbreak{}merge decisions originate externally. Internal triage, evidence verification and approval concern applicability and governed processing of that authoritative outcome, not person matching, golden-record determination, master-person selection or originating merge adjudication.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Correction Requested → HIM Triage → Evidence Verified → Correction Approved → Merge/\allowbreak{}Unlink Executed → Change Broadcasted → Closed



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Correction Requested}}: Externally authoritative correction or merge/\allowbreak{}unlink outcome received for governed application.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{HIM Triage}}: Health Information Manager reviews the received decision/\allowbreak{}outcome and its applicability.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Evidence Verified}}: Authoritative source decision and supporting provenance/\allowbreak{}documentation verified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Correction Approved}}: Governed application of the externally authoritative outcome approved; this does not originate a person-merge decision.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Merge/Unlink Executed}}: External merge/\allowbreak{}unlink consequences applied to Harmonia's managed identifier associations and audit history.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Change Broadcasted}}: Downstream clinical systems notified of merged or rectified identity.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 2.2 Practitioner Verification Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Provider Administration`

HCM-PR-practitioner-verification-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Provider Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the lifecycle of validating, certifying, and periodically re-verifying a healthcare practitioner's professional credentials, registration status, and clinical scope of practice.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Verification Initiated → Regulatory Registry Queried → Credentials Validated → Privileges Endorsed → Active Verified → Expired /\allowbreak{} Suspended



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Verification Initiated}}: New practitioner registration or periodic re-credentialing triggered.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Regulatory Registry Queried}}: Real-time query executed against national registry (e.g., AHPRA).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Credentials Validated}}: Primary qualifications, specialist endorsements, and sanctions checked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Privileges Endorsed}}: Health service medical administration endorses admitting/\allowbreak{}procedural scope.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Active Verified}}: Practitioner verified for clinical ordering and electronic communication.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Expired / Suspended}}: Verification lapses or regulatory sanction triggers privilege suspension.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 3.3 Referral Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Referral Administration`

HCM-PR-referral-progression-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Referral Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the end-to-end operational progression of an incoming clinical referral from receipt through specialist clinical triage, booking, and final service acceptance.



\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: This illustrates a specialist booking/\allowbreak{}attendance pathway; Referral does not universally require acceptance, scheduling, attendance or discharge, or establish delivery, responsibility actually assumed or Transfer of Care. Decline, rejection and redirection remain valid dispositions without invented transition paths. \texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted / Waitlisted}} is a local compound checkpoint, not universal equivalence between acceptance and waitlisting.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Submitted → Intake Validated → Clinically Triaged → Accepted /\allowbreak{} Waitlisted → Scheduled → Consultation Attended → Discharged /\allowbreak{} Rejected   (Illustrative specialist pathway; dispositions vary)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Submitted}}: Electronic referral received from GP or external facility.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Intake Validated}}: Administrative validation of patient details, mandatory fields, and tests.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinically Triaged}}: Senior clinician assigns urgency category (e.g., Cat 1 urgent within 30 days).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted / Waitlisted}}: Referral accepted and placed onto the specialty waitlist.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Scheduled}}: Outpatient appointment allocated and patient notified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation Attended}}: Patient seen; initial specialist assessment completed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharged / Rejected}}: Referral completed and discharged back to primary care, or formally rejected with clinical rationale.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 3.4 Encounter Lifecycle Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Episode & Encounter Administration`

HCM-PR-encounter-lifecycle-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Episode \& Encounter Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the clinical and administrative lifecycle of an acute, emergency, inpatient, or outpatient encounter between a patient and healthcare services.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Planned /\allowbreak{} Booked → Arrived → Triaged /\allowbreak{} Ingested → Active In-Progress → Discharged → Completed /\allowbreak{} Encoded   (Scoped illustration; ON\_LEAVE relationship unresolved)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Planned / Booked}}: Elective admission or clinic appointment scheduled.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Arrived}}: Patient presents at facility or emergency desk.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Triaged / Ingested}}: Clinical triage category assigned; encounter record activated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Active In-Progress}}: Inpatient care, bedside monitoring, and clinical orders actively underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharged}}: Patient clinically discharged; care-place vacated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Completed / Encoded}}: Clinical documentation finalized, ICD/\allowbreak{}DRG coding completed, and encounter legally closed.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: These completion criteria retain their locally described applicability; they do not establish universal signing, legal closure or originating authority over clinical information. Finalisation, signing and legal qualification remain distinct. The relationship with Strategy \texttt{\seqsplit{ON\_LEAVE}}, including applicability and transitions, remains unresolved.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 3.5 Closed-Loop Order Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Order Administration`

HCM-PR-closed-loop-order-progression-pro.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Order Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the rigorous, closed-loop tracking of diagnostic pathology, radiology, and procedural orders from requisition to result correlation, preventing dropped or unfulfilled investigations.



\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: These examples describe a diagnostic/\allowbreak{}procedural progression and do not exclude medication from the broader Order Administration responsibility. Specimen and result checkpoints are scoped. The signed requisition/\allowbreak{}report requirements remain within this illustrated scope; signing is not universally equivalent to finalisation or authority. Result consumption/\allowbreak{}binding does not define originating validity, authority, authorship or legal status.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Requisition Placed → Order Dispatched → Specimen Collected /\allowbreak{} Scheduled → In-Execution → Preliminary Result Bound → Final Result Bound → Closed /\allowbreak{} Verified   (Scoped diagnostic/\allowbreak{}procedural illustration)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Requisition Placed}}: Electronic order created and signed by requesting clinician.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Order Dispatched}}: Order routed and accepted by performing diagnostic service. This local compound checkpoint retains routing and recipient acceptance as distinct facts; dispatch alone establishes neither receipt nor acceptance. Behaviour \texttt{\seqsplit{Received}} is not equated with this checkpoint without evidence.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Collected / Scheduled}}: Bio-specimen collected or imaging appointment booked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Execution}}: Laboratory analysis or diagnostic scanning underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Preliminary Result Bound}}: Critical or interim observations published and linked to order.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Final Result Bound}}: Authoritative diagnostic report signed and bound to order.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Closed / Verified}}: Requesting clinician acknowledges result; order closed. This Order-closure checkpoint does not establish diagnostic-content verification, approval or clinical incorporation.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 3.6 Clinical Document Lifecycle Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinical Record Administration`

HCM-PR-clinical-document-lifecycle-proce.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Record Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the versioning, clinical sign-off, addenda, superseding, and legal status of clinical documents (discharge summaries, specialist letters, advance care directives).



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Draft → Preliminary → Final Signed → Amended /\allowbreak{} Addended → Superseded → Entered-in-Error   (Scoped illustration; no universal document lifecycle)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Draft}}: Incomplete clinical document saved during consultation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Preliminary}}: Document authored pending senior registrar or consultant countersignature.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Final Signed}}: Authoritative clinical document legally signed and published.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Amended / Addended}}: Governed supplementary clinical addendum appended to signed document.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Superseded}}: Entire document replaced by a newer revision; prior version retained for audit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Entered-in-Error}}: Document formally retracted due to wrong patient or invalid content; content struck through with retraction notice.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Final ≠ automatically Final Signed}}. The described signing/\allowbreak{}countersigning and legal qualifications remain local requirements, not a universal document lifecycle. Authorship, attestation, approval, authentication, verification, signature, finalisation, authority and legal qualification remain distinct. Amendment, supersession and entered-in-error are not mandatory stages for every document, and consumer processing does not establish originating authority or legal status.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.7 Theatre Case Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Theatre Operations`

HCM-PR-theatre-case-progression-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Theatre Operations}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the perioperative operational milestones of a surgical procedure within the operating theatre suite.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Case Called → In Anaesthetic Bay → Anaesthesia Commenced → Patient in Theatre → Knife-to-Skin → Procedure Finished → In PACU Recovery → Ward Handover Complete



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Case Called}}: Theatre team requests ward to send patient for surgery.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In Anaesthetic Bay}}: Patient arrives in theatre holding and identity/\allowbreak{}consent verified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Anaesthesia Commenced}}: Anaesthetic induction underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient in Theatre}}: Patient transferred onto operating table.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Knife-to-Skin}}: Surgical incision initiated (operative start).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Procedure Finished}}: Wound closure completed and dressings applied.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In PACU Recovery}}: Patient monitored in post-anaesthesia care unit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Ward Handover Complete}}: Post-operative clinical handover to inpatient ward completed.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.8 Clinic / Operational Queue Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinic & Practice Operations`

HCM-PR-clinic-operational-queue-progress.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinic \& Practice Operations}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the movement and state tracking of outpatients through an ambulatory specialty clinic session.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Scheduled → Patient Arrived → Checked-In → Roomed /\allowbreak{} Pre-Consult → Consultation In-Progress → Consultation Concluded → Departed



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Scheduled}}: Appointment booked on session list.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Arrived}}: Patient enters waiting area.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Checked-In}}: Reception verifies demographics and marks patient ready.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Roomed / Pre-Consult}}: Nursing staff record baseline vitals and room patient.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation In-Progress}}: Clinician actively conducting consultation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation Concluded}}: Clinical discussion finished; follow-up orders placed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Departed}}: Patient checks out and departs clinic facility.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.9 Bed Turnover Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Bed & Care-Place Management`

HCM-PR-bed-turnover-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Bed \& Care-Place Management}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the rapid physical turnover, cleaning, sanitisation, and re-allocation of inpatient and emergency care-places.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Bed Vacated → Cleaning Dispatched → Sanitisation In-Progress → Terminal Cleaning Verified → Bed Ready /\allowbreak{} Available → Bed Allocated /\allowbreak{} Occupied



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Vacated}}: Prior patient discharged or transferred.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Cleaning Dispatched}}: Cleaning job allocated to environmental services team.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Sanitisation In-Progress}}: Ward cleaning or isolation decontamination underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Terminal Cleaning Verified}}: Ward coordinator or supervisor verifies care-place readiness.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Ready / Available}}: Bed marked available for incoming patient allocation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Allocated / Occupied}}: Incoming patient allocated and physically placed in bed.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.10 Operational Work Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Work Allocation & Dispatch`

HCM-PR-operational-work-progression-proc.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Work Allocation \& Dispatch}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the dispatch, assignment, execution, and completion of facility operational jobs (e.g., equipment moves, waste removal, linen supply).



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Work Requested → Queued in Dispatch → Assigned to Worker → Job Accepted → Work In-Progress → Work Completed /\allowbreak{} Aborted



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work Requested}}: Facility support task submitted by clinical unit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Queued in Dispatch}}: Job prioritized in operational queue.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Assigned to Worker}}: Job allocated to specific staff member or team.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Job Accepted}}: Worker acknowledges dispatch on mobile device.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work In-Progress}}: Task actively being executed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work Completed / Aborted}}: Job marked finished or formally cancelled with reason.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.11 Patient Transport Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Patient Transport`

HCM-PR-patient-transport-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Transport}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical portering and transport of patients between hospital departments, wards, diagnostic suites, and external facilities.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Transport Requested → Porter Dispatched → Patient Collected → In-Transit → Delivered at Destination → Clinical Handover Complete



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport Requested}}: Clinical unit books wheelchair, bed, or ambulance transport.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Porter Dispatched}}: Wardsperson assigned and en route to pickup location.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Collected}}: Patient identity verified and transfer initiated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit}}: Patient actively moving through facility corridors or ambulance transit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Delivered at Destination}}: Patient arrives at target diagnostic suite or ward.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Handover Complete}}: Safe custody and clinical briefing transferred to receiving staff.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.12 Specimen Transport Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinical Logistics Coordination`

HCM-PR-specimen-transport-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Logistics Coordination}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical courier chain-of-custody, transport, and delivery of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical biopsies.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Specimen Packaged → Courier Dispatched → Chain-of-Custody Signed → In-Transit (Monitored) → Lab Ingress Received → Specimen Accepted



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Packaged}}: Clinical unit packages bio-sample with barcode manifest.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Courier Dispatched}}: Courier route assigned for pickup.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Chain-of-Custody Signed}}: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit (Monitored)}}: Specimen in transit under temperature/\allowbreak{}time constraints.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Lab Ingress Received}}: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Accepted}}: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 4.13 Discharge Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Discharge Management`

HCM-PR-discharge-progression-process.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Management}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the multidisciplinary coordination of patient discharge planning, pharmacy reconciliation, transport, and community handover.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Discharge Planning Initiated → Clinical Readiness Confirmed → Medications Reconciled → Transport \& Services Booked → Discharge Summary Signed → Physically Departed   (Illustrative preparation; publication, authorisation and exit distinct)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Planning Initiated}}: Estimated Date of Discharge (EDD) set on admission.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Readiness Confirmed}}: Attending medical team declares patient fit for discharge.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Medications Reconciled}}: Hospital pharmacy reconciles and dispenses discharge medications.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport \& Services Booked}}: Community nursing, home equipment, and patient transport booked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Summary Signed}}: Applicable signed summary is available/\allowbreak{}published and may be communicated before departure where the Business behaviour requires it; signing, finalisation, publication and discharge authorisation remain distinct.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Physically Departed}}: Confirmed physical exit triggers departure notifications, updated bed-state communication and finalised-summary dispatch to external care providers under \texttt{\seqsplit{FEAT-HSO-29}}; care-place turnover follows its own responsibility.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Timing reconciliation}: Preparation, information availability/\allowbreak{}publication, applicable discharge authorisation and physical exit are distinct. Earlier preparation/\allowbreak{}communication is permitted; it does not realise a Feature triggered by confirmed exit. This illustrated local pathway establishes neither universal publication timing nor a universal discharge state machine, and adds no inferred publication event or authorisation state.



\item 
\textbf{Preserved uncertainty}: Summary signing and finalisation are not universal equivalents. Detailed applicability, discharge-authority workflows and timing beyond the established preparation/\allowbreak{}confirmed-exit distinction remain unestablished.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

sources.text: ### 6.3 Assurance Process Reporting / Communication
- **Owning Capability**: [Governed Assurance](../../02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance).

HCM-PR-assurance-process-reporting-commu.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Reporting / Communication}}.



\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#governed-assurance}{Governed Assurance}.



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to legitimate recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements, without altering the established assurance outcome or assuming responsibility for the recipient's subsequent action.



\item 
\textbf{Starting Basis}: An already established Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion. This Process does not perform assessment or adjudication, alter or reinterpret the established outcome.



\item 
\textbf{Communication Participation}: Service Guardian participates through \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-outcome-communication}{Service Assurance Outcome Communication}, associated with \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#communicate-service-assurance-outcome}{Communicate Service Assurance Outcome}. No additional Function is introduced to populate this Process.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Reporting /\allowbreak{} Communication is not limited to documentary report production; an appropriate Business Interaction may communicate the outcome without a report document. It assumes no operational response, remediation, escalation, policy/\allowbreak{}compliance response, process improvement, clinical management, clinical judgement or other recipient action. Detailed communication progression and completion semantics remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-01: Managed Entity & Relationship

EC-01.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of managed healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Uniquely identifying core domain entities (Persons, Practitioners, Roles, Organisations, Locations, Services, Devices).



\item 
Resolving and maintaining multi-authority identifier systems and aliases without destructive overwriting.



\item 
Representing and traversing multi-dimensional relationships (affiliations, organizational hierarchies, physical location trees, care team memberships).



\item 
Maintaining referential integrity across interconnected entity graphs.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own physical database relational tables or foreign key constraints (Domain 04/\allowbreak{}07).



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-02: Context Management

EC-02.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Establish, validate, propagate, and preserve the execution, clinical, security, and administrative context within which information and activities have meaning.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Binding the subject of care, encounter, ordering provider, and healthcare service context to in-flight messages and transactions.



\item 
Propagating tamper-evident, attributable security context across asynchronous, multi-hop operational boundaries.



\item 
Ensuring context preservation during cross-protocol transformations across disparate healthcare exchange formats and protocols.



\item 
Detecting and rejecting requests where mandatory operational or clinical context is missing or inconsistent.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Bounded reusable context responsibility may be realised through participation across gateways, activity execution and information-access boundaries. Participation does not transfer semantic ownership.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-03: Managed State & Lifecycle

EC-03.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Govern the current and historical state, effective temporal periods, state transition validations, and lifecycle progression of managed integration artifacts and entities.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Defining and enforcing valid state transition state machines (e.g., \texttt{\seqsplit{REQUESTED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{VALIDATED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{IN\_PROGRESS}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{COMPLETED}}).



\item 
Maintaining temporal validity intervals (effective start and end dates) for relationships, credentials, and states.



\item 
Supporting non-destructive state progression, preserving historical state versions for longitudinal review.



\item 
Rejecting illegal or out-of-order state transitions while accommodating idempotent replay.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not define thread-level mutexes or database transaction isolation levels.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-04: Information Management

EC-04.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Validate, represent, persist, retrieve, version, and manage governed clinical, administrative, and operational information assets.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Validating inbound information structures against canonical information constraints.



\item 
Providing authoritative durable persistence for historical health records and administrative registries.



\item 
Managing active distributed working memory representations for low-latency retrieval.



\item 
Governing document versioning, supersession, amendments, and retractions without data loss.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Architectural Principle}: Enforces the foundational separation between \emph{active distributed state access} and \emph{authoritative durable state preservation} (Axiom AX-05).



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-05: Search & Discovery

EC-05.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Index, search, resolve, filter, and discover information assets, entities, directory endpoints, and healthcare services across the enterprise.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Providing multi-criteria indexed search across complex entity graphs (e.g., find active cardiologists at Location X accepting new referrals).



\item 
Resolving service and practitioner communication endpoints for addressed delivery.



\item 
Supporting bounded, paginated clinical queries across longitudinal patient records.



\item 
Applying dynamic security and consent filters to search results prior to egress.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not dictate specific search engine indexes, inverted index implementations, or SQL query syntaxes.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-06: Policy & Control

EC-06.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Evaluate and enforce security, consent, privacy, and regulatory policies including authority, access control, and information handling rules.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Executing impartial, default-deny policy evaluations for all integration transactions.



\item 
Enforcing Role-Based and Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/\allowbreak{}ABAC) policies.



\item 
Evaluating patient consent directives and privacy restrictions at boundary and query checkpoints.



\item 
Enforcing statutory information disclosure boundaries (e.g., mental health, VIP records).



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Evaluated across boundary gateways, internal bus dispatch, storage interfaces, and presentation layers.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-07: Provenance & Traceability

EC-07.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation history, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end traceability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where required by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction, security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require durable evidentiary recording.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Recording attributable, verifiable origin metadata for information sources, authors, and timestamps.



\item 
Tracking information-significant transformation history and required mapping checkpoints as information crosses system seams.



\item 
Capturing non-PHI operational and security audit trails for regulatory compliance (HIPAA, GDPR).



\item 
Supporting end-to-end transaction tracing across asynchronous processing pipelines.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Participating elements preserve required provenance and audit context according to policy. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Being evidence is contextual, not an intrinsic property of every recorded fact; preservation does not establish an assurance conclusion.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-08: Interoperability & Exchange

EC-08.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Resolve destinations, transform schemas, route, transport, deliver, acknowledge, and coordinate standards-based information exchange across enterprise boundaries.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Providing multi-protocol boundary adaptation for healthcare standards (HL7 v2, FHIR REST, DICOM, secure messaging).



\item 
Executing bidirectional structural and semantic transformations between legacy formats and canonical representations.



\item 
Ensuring reliable addressed delivery and fan-out distribution to external clinical endpoints.



\item 
Processing and distinguishing technical delivery acknowledgements from business acknowledgements.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Boundary Rule}: Egress terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation (Axiom AX-13).



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-09: Event & Subscription

EC-09.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Publish, ingest, correlate, filter, and syndicate events and subscription-driven changes across the enterprise landscape.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Ingesting operational and clinical event triggers from external systems and internal state changes.



\item 
Managing topic- and criteria-based event subscriptions for internal and external consumers.



\item 
Evaluating dynamic subscription filters to match event payloads with interested subscriber criteria.



\item 
Delivering asynchronous event notifications reliably to registered subscribers.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Decoupling Note}: Defined strictly in terms of event publishing, criteria matching, and notification delivery; entirely independent of broker topics, partitions, or queues.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-10: Activity & Execution

EC-10.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Define, instantiate, match, assign, dispatch, supervise, and progress coordinated operational and clinical activity units.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Instantiating operational work items (Work Orders, To Dos, synthetic platform Tasks) in response to triggers.



\item 
Matching and assigning work units to eligible human or automated performers and roles based on policy rules.



\item 
Dispatching work units to their assigned performers with acknowledgement according to the applicable interaction contract.



\item 
Supervising execution progress, tracking timeouts, managing escalations, and handling activity interruptions.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Decoupling Note}: Free of worker threads, thread pools, execution daemons, or specific workflow runtime engines.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-11: Interaction & Experience

EC-11.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Provide contextual interaction between human actors, Harmonia, and enterprise presentation services, including visualization, alerting, and collaboration integration.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Mediating presentation interactions via dedicated backend-for-frontend gateways decoupled from internal databases.



\item 
Rendering clinical timelines, provider directory management interfaces, and operational console dashboards.



\item 
Providing contextual notifications and alerts to human users across web and mobile channels.



\item 
Projecting longitudinal record context into secure multidisciplinary collaboration spaces.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Boundary Note}: Does not absorb the healthcare semantics of Clinical Collaboration or medical documentation. Consumes established identity and security context; does not own authentication, consent, or clinical truth.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-12: Operational Assurance

EC-12.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Ensure concurrency integrity, system resilience, duplicate detection, exception handling, automated recovery, and operational telemetry across platform operations.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Enforcing sliding-window duplicate message detection and idempotent suppression.



\item 
Guaranteeing ingress dual-write safety (durable acceptance before emitting positive application ACK).



\item 
Managing structured failure recovery, exception escalation, and dead-letter isolation.



\item 
Emitting platform telemetry, operational health metrics, and queue processing metrics.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Realized collaboratively across boundary gateways, messaging infrastructure, execution workers, and storage layers.



\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{EC-12 /\allowbreak{} EC-14 Boundary}

EC-12 retains the established scope and responsibilities above. It may contribute directly to generic operational/\allowbreak{}processing assurance, limited to that contribution in the \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved assurance matrix}. It does not own the general semantics of assurance disposition, assurance-specific criteria applicability, evidentiary association, assessment against assurance criteria, adjudication, or independent assurance findings and conclusions. Those distinguishing responsibilities are introduced through EC-14 Service Guardian. Operational health and business-level processing assurance remain distinct; EC-12 is not expanded to absorb EC-14.

sources.text: ### EC-13: Semantic Governance & Conformance

EC-13.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Govern canonical models, schemas, terminologies, value sets, mapping tables, constraint rules, and semantic conformance validation across the enterprise.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Defining and publishing canonical healthcare data models and profile structures.



\item 
Governing clinical terminology mappings, value sets, and concept lookups (SNOMED CT, LOINC).



\item 
Validating inbound and outbound message representations against published semantic rules.



\item 
Governing semantic versioning, deprecation, and backward compatibility across schema revisions.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Component Relationship}: Informs the Calliope strategic logical component, but Calliope is the responsibility centre, not the capability definition.



\end{itemize}

sources.text: ### EC-14: Service Guardian

EC-14.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Service Guardian provides the reusable capability to independently establish whether governed service behaviour, state or outcomes remain within defined assurance expectations by associating applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence with a governed subject, assessing that evidence, adjudicating the assessment, and establishing reportable assurance findings and conclusions.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Supplying assurance-specific semantics for assurance disposition and assurance criteria applicability.



\item 
Associating a governed subject/\allowbreak{}context with applicable criteria and sufficient trustworthy evidence for a particular assurance purpose.



\item 
Assessing evidence against applicable criteria and adjudicating assessed detail to establish reportable findings, exceptions and conclusions.



\item 
Preserving assurance independence, temporal/\allowbreak{}version-specific evidence and criteria applicability, and explicit inability to establish a conclusion where evidence is insufficient.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Supplies the assurance-specific semantics required to bind existing reusable capabilities into governed assurance. It contributes directly to Assurance Design, Assurance Criteria Management and Governed Assurance; direct contribution is not sole realisation. The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved matrix} preserves the contributions of EC-01 through EC-13.



\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own the underlying governed subject, authoritative governance requirements, or source information used as evidence. Does not perform, manage, remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject activity. Does not replace System Operations or EC-12 Operational Assurance, and does not provide Clinical Services Delivery Assurance.



\item 
\textbf{Allocation Boundary}: No strategic logical component, application component, runtime service or implementation construct is allocated EC-14. The catalogue defines a capability, not a software component or deployment boundary.



\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Conceptual Behavioural Sequence}

\textit{RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).}
\begin{quote}
Define Good Behaviour

↓

Gather Evidence

↓

Assess Evidence against Good Behaviour

↓

Adjudicate Assessed Detail

↓

Report
\end{quote}

This sequence explains the capability; it is not an implementation workflow specification or a derived Business Process. “Define Good Behaviour” identifies assurance expectations and criteria; it does not transfer ownership of governing requirements to Service Guardian. Source information ownership remains with its responsible capability; assurance owns its contextual evidentiary association.


The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#health-service-assurance-approved-business-enabling-capabilities}{Business Enabling assurance principles} govern disposition, generic processing assurance, evidence/\allowbreak{}criteria temporality, assessment/\allowbreak{}adjudication, independence, failure/\allowbreak{}recovery and explicit evidence insufficiency. These semantics are not universally reducible to PASS /\allowbreak{} FAIL /\allowbreak{} UNKNOWN and do not imply an assurance information model or persistence mechanism.
